__In\-Specie Distribution to Shareholders in Voluntary Liquidation under the IBC__

*Reference Note, Practice MCQs and Answer Key*

Regulatory Framework  •  Valuation  •  Income\-Tax Treatment  •  Case Law  •  15 MCQs with Key

Jurisdiction: Delhi \(default\)   |   For information and educational purposes only

__Contents__

Part A — Reference Note \(issue, framework, valuation, income\-tax treatment, case digest, guardrails\)

Part B — Practice MCQs \(15 questions\)

Part C — Answer Key with Rationale & Statutory / Case Anchors

__PART A__

__Reference Note__

# __1\.  Issue__

Whether, in the voluntary liquidation of a solvent company under Section 59 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 \(“IBC” / “Code”\), shares of an unlisted company held by the company under liquidation may be distributed to its shareholders *in specie* — that is, in their actual form — without being sold through the Schedule I e\-auction process; and the attendant valuation and income\-tax consequences\.

# __2\.  Short Answer__

Yes\. Unlisted shares \(and, as the case law shows, even immovable property\) may be distributed to shareholders *in specie* without routing them through e\-auction, provided the statutory conditions in Regulation 35\(3\) read with Regulation 31 of the IBBI \(Voluntary Liquidation Process\) Regulations, 2017 are met and the distribution is supported by a registered\-valuer fair value and made strictly in accordance with the shareholders’ entitlement\. The e\-auction machinery under Schedule I is a mode of *sale*; an in\-specie distribution is not a sale but a distribution of the asset itself, so that machinery is not attracted\.

# __3\.  Statutory and Regulatory Framework__

The e\-auction process under Schedule I is the default mode of realisation by *sale*\. In\-specie distribution is conceptually distinct: the asset is handed over in its existing form rather than converted to cash\. Two provisions enable it in a Section 59 process, with a mirror provision governing the corporate\-liquidation stream:

## __Clause\-map__

__Aspect__

__Voluntary Liquidation — VL Regulations, 2017__

__Corporate / CIRP\-origin Liquidation — Liquidation Regulations, 2016__

__Statute__

Section 59, IBC

Section 33 / 35, IBC

__Distribution provision__

Regulation 35 — esp\. Reg\. 35\(3\) \(distribution of an un\-saleable asset among stakeholders\)

Regulation 37 \(distribution of un\-saleable asset among stakeholders\)

__Mode of realisation / sale__

Regulation 31 — liquidator may value and sell property in any manner and mode approved by the corporate person

Regulation 32 \+ Schedule I \(e\-auction is the default mode\); Reg\. 33 permits private sale with reasons

__Test for in\-specie route__

Asset that cannot be readily or advantageously sold due to its peculiar nature or other special circumstances

Same statutory wording

__Approving authority__

Approval of the corporate person \(members\); NCLT records/confirms at dissolution u/s 59\(7\)

Permission of the Adjudicating Authority \(NCLT\) is required

__Distribution timeline__

Realisation proceeds to be distributed within six months of receipt — Reg\. 35\(1\)

As per model timeline / Reg\. 47 read with Reg\. 37

Key structural distinction: in __voluntary__ liquidation the trigger for in\-specie distribution is approval of the *corporate person* \(the members\), whereas in __corporate/CIRP\-origin__ liquidation it requires permission of the *Adjudicating Authority*\. In practice, in voluntary matters the NCLT records and effectively confirms the in\-specie distribution at the Section 59\(7\) dissolution stage\.

# __4\.  Valuation Framework__

- A __registered\-valuer__ report \(under the Companies \(Registered Valuers and Valuation\) Rules, 2017 / IBBI framework\) is effectively indispensable\. Regulation 3 of the VL Regulations already requires an asset valuation for the declaration of solvency\.
- The fair value fixes \(i\) the fairness of the pro\-rata distribution across members, and \(ii\) the “market value on the date of distribution” that drives the income\-tax computation under Sections 46\(2\) and 55\(2\)\(b\)\(iii\)\.
- For unlisted shares, expect NAV and DCF \(and, where relevant, comparable\-company\) approaches\. Keep the *commercial* FMV in the registered\-valuer report distinct from the *tax* FMV under Rule 11UA — Rule 11UA governs Section 56\(2\)\(x\) situations, whereas Section 46\(2\) speaks of actual “market value\.” Where the two diverge materially, document the reasons\.
- The distribution must be at fair value and strictly in accordance with entitlement / the Section 53 waterfall\. In\-specie cannot be used to move value out below fair value or to the wrong hands\.

# __5\.  Income\-Tax Treatment__

## __\(a\)  Company side — the core advantage__

Under __Section 46\(1\)__, where assets are distributed to shareholders *on liquidation*, such distribution shall not be regarded as a transfer by the company; hence there is no capital gain to the company\. This is the decisive contrast with a sell\-then\-distribute route: if the liquidator *sells* the shares/property and distributes cash, that sale is a transfer and the company bears capital\-gains tax\. \(Note that the section says “on liquidation,” not “in liquidation” — distribution should sit at or near completion\.\)

## __\(b\)  Shareholder side — two layers__

- __Deemed dividend — Sec\. 2\(22\)\(c\): __the distribution is a deemed dividend to the extent of accumulated profits \(capitalised or not\)\. Post\-abolition of DDT \(Finance Act, 2020\) it is taxable in the shareholder’s hands at applicable rates, with TDS u/s 194 \(residents\) or u/s 195 / DTAA \(non\-residents\)\.
- __Capital gains — Sec\. 46\(2\): __the shareholder is chargeable on the money received or the market value of assets on the date of distribution, reduced by the amount assessed as dividend u/s 2\(22\)\(c\); that sum is the deemed full value of consideration for Section 48, from which the cost of acquisition of the *shares extinguished* is deducted\. Holding period: Sec\. 2\(42A\) excludes the period after the liquidation commencement date\. LTCG on unlisted shares is 12\.5% without indexation post\-23\.07\.2024 \(Finance \(No\. 2\) Act, 2024\)\.

## __\(c\)  On subsequent sale by the shareholder__

Under __Section 55\(2\)\(b\)\(iii\)__, the cost of acquisition of the asset received in specie is its market value on the date of distribution, with a fresh holding period from that date — which is why fixing the date\-of\-distribution FMV matters twice over\.

## __\(d\)  Other levies and a caution__

- __Section 56\(2\)\(x\): __as 46\(2\) is a specific charge against extinguishment of shares, the mainstream view is that 56\(2\)\(x\) does not apply; but if the FMV distributed to a member *exceeds* his rateable entitlement, the excess is exposed to a 56\(2\)\(x\) argument\. Keep the distribution strictly pro\-rata\.
- __GST: __an in\-specie distribution to shareholders is not a supply for consideration and generally does not attract GST, whereas a sale would\. Prior GST dues must nonetheless be cleared\.
- __Stamp duty: __unlike the UK SDLT position, an in\-specie transfer of immovable property in India attracts stamp duty under the relevant State Stamp Act; for shares, factor share\-transfer/transmission stamp duty\. Model this as a real cost\.

## __\(e\)  Worked illustration — Section 46\(2\)__

Assume ABC Investments Pvt\. Ltd\. \(unlisted, solvent\) in voluntary liquidation; sole asset is 10,000 unlisted equity shares of XYZ Pvt\. Ltd\. distributed in specie to its 100% shareholder, Mr\. A\. Figures are illustrative\.

__Particulars__

__A\.  Company side — ABC Investments Pvt\. Ltd\. \(in liquidation\)__

__B\.  Shareholder side — Mr\. A \(100% holder of ABC\)__

# __6\.  Judicial and Quasi\-Judicial Precedents__

__Case__

__Forum & Citation__

__Ratio / Relevance__

__Nu\-Foam Rubber Industries Pvt\. Ltd\., In re__

NCLT, New Delhi Bench — C\.P\.\(IB\)/469/ND/2023, order dated 02\.07\.2024 \(Member \(T\): Dr\. Sanjeev Ranjan\)

Flagship\. In a Sec\. 59 voluntary liquidation, two immovable properties \(flats at Gurgaon\) were distributed to shareholders in specie in their 56:44 shareholding ratio under Reg\. 35\(3\), with approval of the corporate person; dissolution allowed\.

__Vinod Radhakrishnan Nair v\. EPFO__

NCLT, Chennai Bench

Where an asset \(NRRA / PUFE proceeds\) could not be sold despite repeated auctions, NCLT approved distribution of the unsold asset among stakeholders — Reg\. 37 stream\. Establishes distribution as a legitimate alternative to sale\.

__Oriental Bank of Commerce v\. AVJ Infrastructure Pvt\. Ltd\.__

NCLT, New Delhi — 2026 TAXSCAN \(NCLT\) 144; IA\(IBC\)/Dis\./40\(PB\)/2025, order dated 11\.05\.2026

Assignment / distribution of NRRAs does not obstruct dissolution where no further realisable assets remain for distribution u/s 53\. Non\-cash realisation routes are compatible with a clean dissolution\.

__R\.K\. Industries \(Unit\-II\) LLP__

Supreme Court of India

Liquidator’s discretion over the mode of realisation: auction is not the exclusive path; a private / alternative mode may be adopted with NCLT sanction \(Reg\. 33 gives ample latitude\)\. Supports the in\-specie logic by analogy\.

__Leo Edibles & Fats Ltd\. v\. Tax Recovery Officer \(Central\), I\.T\. Dept\., Hyderabad__

High Court of Telangana — W\.P\. No\. 8560/2018

IBC\-vs\-Income\-Tax interface where property moves out of a company in liquidation; the purchaser \(not the liquidator\) is to credit TDS\. Relevant when clearing IT attachments/charges before transferring property to shareholders\.

__CIT v\. Jaykrishna Harivallabhdas__

High Court of Gujarat — judgment dated 14\.02\.1997

Tax anchor\. On liquidation the shareholder’s right to surplus is a capital asset and its extinguishment is a transfer; Sec\. 46\(2\) read with Sec\. 48 governs the computation, and a capital loss can arise where receipts fall below cost\.

__Note on use: __NCLT bench orders are fact\-specific and not always carried by the usual citators\. Before relying on the Nu\-Foam and NRRA orders in an opinion or teaching deck, pull the signed PDFs from the NCLT portal and lock the paragraph pin\-cites\. R\.K\. Industries and Jaykrishna Harivallabhdas are cited for mode\-of\-sale discretion and shareholder capital\-gains mechanics respectively, rather than for in\-specie\-to\-shareholders per se\.

# __7\.  Practical Guardrails__

- Obtain a registered\-valuer FMV as on the date of distribution and retain the working\.
- Distribute strictly pro\-rata to entitlement and in the Section 53 order; record corporate\-person approval under Reg\. 31 / 35\(3\)\.
- Have the in\-specie distribution confirmed by the NCLT at the Section 59\(7\) dissolution stage\.
- Clear GST dues; assess and provide for stamp duty on any immovable property or share transfer\.
- Compute and, where applicable, deduct TDS on the deemed\-dividend component; issue Form 15CA/15CB and comply with FEMA \(NDI\) Rules for any non\-resident shareholder\.
- Avoid any transfer without consideration or below fair value — such transfers have been ordered to be restored\.

__PART B__

__Practice MCQs \(15 Questions\)__

__Q1\. __Distributing an asset to shareholders in specie in a Section 59 voluntary liquidation, instead of selling it, means:

__a\)  __The Schedule I e\-auction process must still be completed before the asset is handed over\.

__b\)  __The liquidator must obtain SEBI approval before the hand\-over\.

__c\)  __The asset is handed to shareholders in its existing form, and the Schedule I e\-auction machinery \(a mode of sale\) is not attracted\.

__d\)  __The distribution is automatically void for want of a public auction\.

__Q2\. __In a voluntary liquidation, the provision that permits the liquidator to distribute among the stakeholders an asset that cannot be readily or advantageously sold is:

__a\)  __Regulation 35\(3\) of the IBBI \(Voluntary Liquidation Process\) Regulations, 2017\.

__b\)  __Regulation 32 of the Liquidation Process Regulations, 2016\.

__c\)  __Section 53 of the IBC\.

__d\)  __Regulation 14 of the IBBI \(Voluntary Liquidation Process\) Regulations, 2017\.

__Q3\. __The statutory test for taking the in\-specie route under Regulation 35\(3\) is that the asset:

__a\)  __Has a book value below Rs\. 1 crore\.

__b\)  __Is fully depreciated in the books\.

__c\)  __Is situated outside India\.

__d\)  __Cannot be readily or advantageously sold due to its peculiar nature or other special circumstances\.

__Q4\. __Under Regulation 31 of the IBBI \(Voluntary Liquidation Process\) Regulations, 2017, the liquidator may value and sell the property of the corporate person:

__a\)  __Only through an e\-auction under Schedule I\.

__b\)  __In any manner and through any mode approved by the corporate person\.

__c\)  __Only with the prior approval of the IBBI\.

__d\)  __Only through a recognised stock exchange\.

__Q5\. __Whose approval is the primary trigger for an in\-specie distribution in a voluntary liquidation, as distinct from a corporate/CIRP\-origin liquidation?

__a\)  __The corporate person \(the members\)\.

__b\)  __The Adjudicating Authority, by prior permission in every case\.

__c\)  __The Reserve Bank of India\.

__d\)  __The Committee of Creditors\.

__Q6\. __In a corporate/CIRP\-origin liquidation, the mirror provision — Regulation 37 of the IBBI \(Liquidation Process\) Regulations, 2016 — permits distribution of an un\-saleable asset among stakeholders only:

__a\)  __Without any approval whatsoever\.

__b\)  __With the approval of the Reserve Bank of India\.

__c\)  __With the permission of the Adjudicating Authority\.

__d\)  __After exactly three failed auctions in every case\.

__Q7\. __Can unlisted equity shares held by a company under voluntary liquidation be distributed to its shareholders in specie?

__a\)  __No; shares must always be sold through e\-auction\.

__b\)  __Only if the shares are listed on a recognised exchange\.

__c\)  __Only with a SEBI takeover exemption\.

__d\)  __Yes; illiquid unlisted shares fit the “peculiar nature” test, subject to corporate\-person approval and a registered\-valuer fair value\.

__Q8\. __In an in\-specie distribution, the fair value fixed by a registered valuer as on the date of distribution matters because it:

__a\)  __Only affects the liquidator’s remuneration\.

__b\)  __Fixes the fairness of the pro\-rata distribution and the “market value on the date of distribution” that drives the income\-tax computation\.

__c\)  __Is required only for listed securities\.

__d\)  __Has no bearing on the tax position\.

__Q9\. __Where the assets of a company are distributed to its shareholders on its liquidation, under Section 46\(1\) of the Income\-tax Act, 1961 such distribution:

__a\)  __Is not regarded as a transfer by the company; hence no capital gain arises to the company\.

__b\)  __Is treated as a transfer by the company, attracting capital gains in the company’s hands\.

__c\)  __Attracts GST in the company’s hands\.

__d\)  __Is fully exempt in the shareholder’s hands as well\.

__Q10\. __On a company’s liquidation, the distribution to shareholders is treated as a deemed dividend under Section 2\(22\)\(c\):

__a\)  __On the entire amount distributed, irrespective of profits\.

__b\)  __Only if the company was listed\.

__c\)  __Never — liquidation distributions are always purely capital\.

__d\)  __To the extent of the accumulated profits of the company \(whether capitalised or not\) immediately before liquidation\.

__Q11\. __Under Section 46\(2\), the “full value of consideration” for the shareholder’s capital\-gains computation is:

__a\)  __The face value of the extinguished shares\.

__b\)  __The money received plus the market value of other assets on the date of distribution, as reduced by the amount assessed as deemed dividend under Section 2\(22\)\(c\)\.

__c\)  __The book value of the assets received\.

__d\)  __Nil in every case\.

__Q12\. __When a shareholder subsequently sells an asset received in specie on liquidation, its cost of acquisition under Section 55\(2\)\(b\)\(iii\) is:

__a\)  __Nil\.

__b\)  __The original cost in the hands of the liquidated company\.

__c\)  __The market value of the asset on the date of distribution\.

__d\)  __The face value of the extinguished shares\.

__Q13\. __On an in\-specie distribution to shareholders in a voluntary liquidation, the position on GST and stamp duty is:

__a\)  __It is generally not a supply for consideration \(no GST, unlike a sale\), but an in\-specie transfer of immovable property attracts stamp duty under the relevant State Stamp Act\.

__b\)  __Both GST and stamp duty are wholly inapplicable\.

__c\)  __GST applies but no stamp duty is payable in India\.

__d\)  __Both apply exactly as on an ordinary third\-party sale\.

__Q14\. __In which order did the NCLT permit distribution of immovable property to shareholders in specie in their shareholding ratio in a voluntary liquidation?

__a\)  __Swiss Ribbons Pvt\. Ltd\. v\. Union of India\.

__b\)  __Ghanashyam Mishra & Sons v\. Edelweiss ARC\.

__c\)  __Essar Steel India Ltd\. \(Committee of Creditors\) v\. Satish Kumar Gupta\.

__d\)  __Nu\-Foam Rubber Industries Pvt\. Ltd\., In re \(NCLT, New Delhi\) — two Gurgaon flats distributed to shareholders in the 56:44 ratio under Reg\. 35\(3\)\.

__Q15\. __On distribution of surplus/assets to shareholders in a voluntary liquidation, the correct position on Tax Deducted at Source \(TDS\) is:

__a\)  __TDS is mandatory under all circumstances on the entire distribution\.

__b\)  __TDS may be attracted on the deemed\-dividend component under Section 2\(22\)\(c\) — Section 194 for residents and Section 195 / DTAA for non\-residents; the IBBI clarification removes only the NOC/NDC requirement, not TDS\.

__c\)  __No TDS is ever required in a liquidation\.

__d\)  __TDS applies only where the distribution is made in cash\.

__PART C__

__Answer Key with Rationale & Anchors__

__Q1\. Distributing an asset to shareholders in specie in a Section 59 voluntary liquidation, instead of selling it, means:__

__Correct answer: c\) __*The asset is handed to shareholders in its existing form, and the Schedule I e\-auction machinery \(a mode of sale\) is not attracted\.*

__Rationale: __In\-specie distribution is a distribution of the asset itself, not a sale; Schedule I governs the mode of sale and is therefore not triggered\.

__Anchor: __*Schedule I r/w Reg\. 31 & 35\(3\), VL Regulations, 2017*

__Q2\. In a voluntary liquidation, the provision that permits the liquidator to distribute among the stakeholders an asset that cannot be readily or advantageously sold is:__

__Correct answer: a\) __*Regulation 35\(3\) of the IBBI \(Voluntary Liquidation Process\) Regulations, 2017\.*

__Rationale: __Reg\. 35\(3\) expressly enables in\-specie distribution of an un\-saleable asset with the approval of the corporate person\.

__Anchor: __*Reg\. 35\(3\), VL Regulations, 2017*

__Q3\. The statutory test for taking the in\-specie route under Regulation 35\(3\) is that the asset:__

__Correct answer: d\) __*Cannot be readily or advantageously sold due to its peculiar nature or other special circumstances\.*

__Rationale: __The regulation uses the phrase “cannot be readily or advantageously sold due to its peculiar nature or other special circumstances\.” Illiquid unlisted shares typically satisfy this\.

__Anchor: __*Reg\. 35\(3\), VL Regulations, 2017 \(text of the test\)*

__Q4\. Under Regulation 31 of the IBBI \(Voluntary Liquidation Process\) Regulations, 2017, the liquidator may value and sell the property of the corporate person:__

__Correct answer: b\) __*In any manner and through any mode approved by the corporate person\.*

__Rationale: __Reg\. 31 confers wide latitude on the mode of realisation, subject to approval of the corporate person; read with Reg\. 35\(3\) it supports the in\-specie route\.

__Anchor: __*Reg\. 31, VL Regulations, 2017*

__Q5\. Whose approval is the primary trigger for an in\-specie distribution in a voluntary liquidation, as distinct from a corporate/CIRP\-origin liquidation?__

__Correct answer: a\) __*The corporate person \(the members\)\.*

__Rationale: __In voluntary liquidation the trigger is approval of the corporate person; the NCLT records/confirms it at the Section 59\(7\) dissolution stage\.

__Anchor: __*Reg\. 31 & 35\(3\) r/w s\. 59\(7\), IBC*

__Q6\. In a corporate/CIRP\-origin liquidation, the mirror provision — Regulation 37 of the IBBI \(Liquidation Process\) Regulations, 2016 — permits distribution of an un\-saleable asset among stakeholders only:__

__Correct answer: c\) __*With the permission of the Adjudicating Authority\.*

__Rationale: __Reg\. 37 of the Liquidation Regulations, 2016 requires permission of the Adjudicating Authority — the key structural difference from the voluntary\-liquidation route\.

__Anchor: __*Reg\. 37, Liquidation Process Regulations, 2016*

__Q7\. Can unlisted equity shares held by a company under voluntary liquidation be distributed to its shareholders in specie?__

__Correct answer: d\) __*Yes; illiquid unlisted shares fit the “peculiar nature” test, subject to corporate\-person approval and a registered\-valuer fair value\.*

__Rationale: __Unlisted, closely\-held shares generally have no ready market and fall within Reg\. 35\(3\); the practice is confirmed by NCLT at dissolution\.

__Anchor: __*Reg\. 35\(3\), VL Regulations, 2017*

__Q8\. In an in\-specie distribution, the fair value fixed by a registered valuer as on the date of distribution matters because it:__

__Correct answer: b\) __*Fixes the fairness of the pro\-rata distribution and the “market value on the date of distribution” that drives the income\-tax computation\.*

__Rationale: __The date\-of\-distribution FMV anchors both distributional fairness and the tax computation\.

__Anchor: __*Companies \(Registered Valuers and Valuation\) Rules, 2017; ss\. 46\(2\) & 55\(2\)\(b\)\(iii\), Income\-tax Act, 1961*

__Q9\. Where the assets of a company are distributed to its shareholders on its liquidation, under Section 46\(1\) of the Income\-tax Act, 1961 such distribution:__

__Correct answer: a\) __*Is not regarded as a transfer by the company; hence no capital gain arises to the company\.*

__Rationale: __Sec\. 46\(1\) excludes the distribution from “transfer” for the company\. Contrast: if the liquidator sells the asset and distributes cash, that sale IS a transfer and the company is taxed — the core reason in\-specie is preferred\.

__Anchor: __*s\. 46\(1\), Income\-tax Act, 1961*

__Q10\. On a company’s liquidation, the distribution to shareholders is treated as a deemed dividend under Section 2\(22\)\(c\):__

__Correct answer: d\) __*To the extent of the accumulated profits of the company \(whether capitalised or not\) immediately before liquidation\.*

__Rationale: __Sec\. 2\(22\)\(c\) deems the distribution a dividend to the extent of accumulated profits\. Post\-DDT abolition \(FA 2020\) it is taxable in the shareholder’s hands\.

__Anchor: __*s\. 2\(22\)\(c\), Income\-tax Act, 1961*

__Q11\. Under Section 46\(2\), the “full value of consideration” for the shareholder’s capital\-gains computation is:__

__Correct answer: b\) __*The money received plus the market value of other assets on the date of distribution, as reduced by the amount assessed as deemed dividend under Section 2\(22\)\(c\)\.*

__Rationale: __From this deemed full value of consideration, the cost of acquisition of the shares extinguished is deducted \(s\. 48\) to arrive at the capital gain\.

__Anchor: __*s\. 46\(2\) r/w s\. 48, Income\-tax Act, 1961*

__Q12\. When a shareholder subsequently sells an asset received in specie on liquidation, its cost of acquisition under Section 55\(2\)\(b\)\(iii\) is:__

__Correct answer: c\) __*The market value of the asset on the date of distribution\.*

__Rationale: __The FMV taken under s\. 46\(2\) becomes the cost under s\. 55\(2\)\(b\)\(iii\); the holding period runs afresh from the date of distribution \(see also s\. 2\(42A\)\)\.

__Anchor: __*s\. 55\(2\)\(b\)\(iii\); s\. 2\(42A\), Income\-tax Act, 1961*

__Q13\. On an in\-specie distribution to shareholders in a voluntary liquidation, the position on GST and stamp duty is:__

__Correct answer: a\) __*It is generally not a supply for consideration \(no GST, unlike a sale\), but an in\-specie transfer of immovable property attracts stamp duty under the relevant State Stamp Act\.*

__Rationale: __In\-specie distribution is not a taxable supply \(prior GST dues must still be cleared\); Indian stamp duty on immovable property \(and share transfer/transmission\) remains a real cost — unlike the UK SDLT position\.

__Anchor: __*CGST Act, 2017 \(scope of “supply”\); relevant State Stamp Act*

__Q14\. In which order did the NCLT permit distribution of immovable property to shareholders in specie in their shareholding ratio in a voluntary liquidation?__

__Correct answer: d\) __*Nu\-Foam Rubber Industries Pvt\. Ltd\., In re \(NCLT, New Delhi\) — two Gurgaon flats distributed to shareholders in the 56:44 ratio under Reg\. 35\(3\)\.*

__Rationale: __The leading Indian authority on immovable\-property in\-specie distribution in a Section 59 process \(pull the signed PDF to lock the paragraph pin\-cite\)\.

__Anchor: __*Nu\-Foam Rubber Industries Pvt\. Ltd\., In re, NCLT New Delhi, C\.P\.\(IB\)/469/ND/2023, order dated 02\.07\.2024*

__Q15\. On distribution of surplus/assets to shareholders in a voluntary liquidation, the correct position on Tax Deducted at Source \(TDS\) is:__

__Correct answer: b\) __*TDS may be attracted on the deemed\-dividend component under Section 2\(22\)\(c\) — Section 194 for residents and Section 195 / DTAA for non\-residents; the IBBI clarification removes only the NOC/NDC requirement, not TDS\.*

__Rationale: __Corrected version of the bank’s Q708\. The IBBI Circular dated 15\.11\.2021 dispenses with the IT NOC in voluntary liquidation; it does not switch off TDS on the deemed\-dividend portion\.

__Anchor: __*ss\. 194 & 195, Income\-tax Act, 1961; s\. 178 r/w IBBI Circular IBBI/LIQ/45/2021 dated 15\.11\.2021*
